_README:
Bahrain National Terrorism List (قائمة الإرهاب الوطنية لمملكة البحرين). Source: Cabinet Resolution No. (01-2741) of 11 March 2024, published as Official Gazette Supplement No. 3739 (28 March 2024) by the Legislation & Legal Opinion Commission, https://www.lloc.gov.bh/PDF/RNCAB0124.pdf - cross-confirmed as the correct primary source via Wikipedia's own citation for 'List of organizations designated as terrorist by Bahrain'. Fetched and extracted 2026-09-27. 

BACKGROUND: an earlier session (documented elsewhere in this registry) attempted this same PDF, fetched it successfully, but found the Arabic text extraction corrupted and correctly declined to guess at corrupted names - leaving this source unresolved rather than risking a mangled sanctions screen. This session re-attempted extraction using pdftotext -layout (poppler-utils) rather than a generic fetch-and-render, with materially better results, but genuine corruption (a spurious replacement character, U+FFFD, and in some cases a literal inserted mid-word space) was still present in the raw extraction - this was not simply a clean success. 

METHODOLOGY: (1) structural validation - the document's own preamble states it is updating an earlier list (Gazette No. 3649, 11 Jan 2023) by adding 15 individuals + 8 entities + 1 vessel, but the document BODY prints the resulting FULL cumulative list, which parsed to exactly 208 individuals, 172 entities, and 7 vessels - an exact match to this same source's figures as already cited elsewhere in this registry from independent prior research, which is itself a strong cross-check that no entries were silently dropped or duplicated. (2) corruption remediation - of 387 total entries, 369 (95%) were clean after mechanically stripping the U+FFFD artifact character (verified across many entries, including several independently, publicly checkable names that decoded correctly: Yusuf al-Qaradawi, Hassan Nasrallah, Qasem Soleimani, Khalifa Mohammed Turki Al-Subaie). The remaining 18 entries had a second defect (an inserted mid-word space, distinct from U+FFFD) and were resolved individually, using only in-document evidence: a clean restatement of the same name/word elsewhere in that entry's own alias list; a standard boilerplate phrase (شركة/'company', استيراد وتصدير/'import and export', معروف باسم/'known as') confirmed clean dozens of times elsewhere in this exact document; or an explicit English name given directly in the same entry (used as authoritative where present). Two entries (individual #106, one alias element each in two places) had NO clean in-document resolution and were left explicitly omitted rather than guessed - see each affected entry's verification_note. 

Every one of the 12 entries that required this kind of reconstruction carries its own verification_note documenting exactly which mechanism was used, so a reviewer can check the reasoning against the primary source PDF directly rather than take it on faith. Nationality and location annotations, where the source PDF states them, are preserved inline in the name field exactly as printed (e.g. '(قطري)'/Qatari, '- متواجد في تركيا'/located in Turkey) rather than parsed into a separate structured field, since the source's own phrasing for these varies entry to entry and forcing it into a fixed schema risked introducing new errors.
decision: Cabinet Resolution No. (01-2741), 11 March 2024 - Official Gazette Supplement No. 3739, 28 March 2024
